## Notes (human, preserved verbatim on regeneration)

<!-- bm-human:begin -->
**One thing is waiting on Khalil, and the window closes.**

The repository is holding still on purpose. A release commit for version 3.3.1
is on main and pushed, and it has no tag yet. This project's own version law
says a release commit the tree moves past before its tag is cut is retired
permanently and can never be tagged later. Two earlier releases died that way
on a single day.

So: cut the tag before anything else commits to this repository.

    git tag -a v3.3.1 -m "BrotherMode 3.3.1: the integrity check passes on a correct install" && git push origin v3.3.1

Why the release exists: version 3.3.0, the version this project tells people to
install, shipped a checksum file describing a file the release does not
contain. The one command this project offers for answering "is my copy the copy
you published" therefore reported a failure on a CORRECT install. Nothing in
the engine was wrong. The manifest was written against a tree that still held
that path.

The fix is proven the way a user meets it: a fresh clone of the release commit
runs the integrity check and gets PASSED, where 3.3.0 gets FAILED.

Read next: 01-HANDOVER.md for the state, 04-NEXT-LOOPS-PRIORITIZED.md for what
follows the tag.
